label: lf-standards-eu-uk
topic: EU and UK reaction-to-fire classes (A1-F) with numeric thresholds, and the class required of timber / bio-based wall and ceiling linings, from open official sources
summary:
The Euroclass thresholds A1-F, the smoke and droplet sub-classes, the UK lining requirements and the no-test class for cross-laminated timber are all confirmed from open official sources; ISO 5660 and standard edition years are not.

Sources opened: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/364 (annex, via legislation.gov.uk, because the EUR-Lex HTML link returned only a journal header), Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2293 (annex), and Approved Document B Volume 2 (gov.uk PDF, text extracted locally and read directly).

One caveat on the 2016/364 numbers: they reached me through the fetch tool's summariser, which paraphrased the table and said it kept numbers and units exact. I did not see the raw table bytes, so re-check them against the annex before putting them in a record.

**Main-class thresholds (all CONFIRMED-OPEN-SOURCE, 2016/364 Table 1):**

| Class | SBI test (EN 13823) | Small-flame test (EN ISO 11925-2) | Other |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | none | none | Furnace: temperature rise <= 30 C, mass loss <= 50 %, no sustained flaming. Calorific potential <= 2.0 MJ/kg (<= 1.4 MJ/m2 for internal non-substantial components) |
| A2 | FIGRA <= 120 W/s, THR600s <= 7.5 MJ, no flame spread to specimen edge | none | Furnace: temperature rise <= 50 C, mass loss <= 50 %, flaming <= 20 s; or calorific potential <= 3.0 MJ/kg (<= 4.0 MJ/m2 for non-substantial components) |
| B | FIGRA <= 120 W/s, THR600s <= 7.5 MJ, no flame spread to edge | Fs <= 150 mm within 60 s (30 s exposure) | |
| C | FIGRA <= 250 W/s, THR600s <= 15 MJ, no flame spread to edge | Fs <= 150 mm within 60 s (30 s exposure) | |
| D | FIGRA <= 750 W/s | Fs <= 150 mm within 60 s (30 s exposure) | |
| E | none | Fs <= 150 mm within 20 s (15 s exposure) | |
| F | none | Fs > 150 mm within 20 s | Approved Document B words it as "fails to attain class E" |

**Sub-classes (CONFIRMED-OPEN-SOURCE):**
- **Smoke:** s1 is SMOGRA <= 30 m2/s2 and TSP600s <= 50 m2; s2 is SMOGRA <= 180 m2/s2 and TSP600s <= 200 m2; s3 is neither.
- **Droplets:** d0 is no flaming droplets within 600 s; d1 is none lasting longer than 10 s; d2 is neither.

**UK lining requirements (CONFIRMED-OPEN-SOURCE, Approved Document B Vol 2, Table 6.1, read directly):**
- Small rooms (up to 4 m2 residential, 30 m2 non-residential): D-s3, d2.
- Other rooms, including garages: C-s3, d2.
- Other circulation spaces: B-s3, d2.
- Paragraph 6.4 lets part of a room's walls drop to D-s3, d2, up to half the floor area, capped at 20 m2 residential or 60 m2 non-residential.

**Timber (CONFIRMED-OPEN-SOURCE, 2017/2293 Table 1):** cross-laminated timber (>= 18 mm layers, >= 350 kg/m3, >= 54 mm thick) and laminated veneer lumber (>= 3 mm veneers, >= 400 kg/m3, >= 18 mm thick) are deemed D-s2, d0 without testing.

My inference, not a quoted statement: plain timber at class D meets the UK guidance only in small rooms or within the paragraph 6.4 partial-wall allowance. Ordinary rooms need class C and circulation spaces class B, which means treatment or coating, or a tested product.

**UNCONFIRMED:**
- Edition years of EN 13501-1, EN 13823, EN ISO 11925-2, EN ISO 1182 and EN ISO 1716. Neither the regulation annex nor the passages of Approved Document B I read state them.
- Anything on ISO 5660 (cone calorimeter). I opened no source for it. It does not appear among the test methods in 2016/364 Table 1, so it is not a Euroclass criterion.
- Approved Document B Volume 1 (dwellings) lining table: not opened.
- Flooring classes (A1fl to Ffl, 2016/364 Table 2): not extracted.

Approved Document B edition as stated on gov.uk: "2019 edition incorporating 2020, 2022, 2025 and 2026 amendments collated with 2029 amendments". The standards list flags a BS EN 13501-1 related entry as "Effective until 1 September 2029", which I did not read in context.

key_claims: Euroclass main thresholds (2016/364): B = FIGRA <= 120 W/s and THR600s <= 7.5 MJ; C = FIGRA <= 250 W/s and THR600s <= 15 MJ; D = FIGRA <= 750 W/s; B, C and D also need Fs <= 150 mm within 60 s; E = Fs <= 150 mm within 20 s; F = fails E.
Smoke: s1 = SMOGRA <= 30 m2/s2 and TSP600s <= 50 m2; s2 = SMOGRA <= 180 m2/s2 and TSP600s <= 200 m2. Droplets: d0 none in 600 s; d1 none longer than 10 s.
UK Approved Document B Vol 2 Table 6.1: linings D-s3,d2 in small rooms (4 m2 residential / 30 m2 non-residential), C-s3,d2 in other rooms, B-s3,d2 in circulation spaces.

Cross-laminated timber and laminated veneer lumber are deemed D-s2,d0 without testing (EU 2017/2293), so plain timber linings fall one or two classes short of what UK guidance asks for in ordinary rooms and corridors.
Standard edition years and anything on ISO 5660 are UNCONFIRMED from open sources in the time available.
lay_summary: Europe and the UK grade building materials by how much they feed a fire, from A1 (does not burn, like stone) down to F (burns easily or was never tested).
The grade comes from tests: a small flame held on the material, and a bigger burner in a room corner that measures how fast the fire grows and how much heat comes out.
The law gives exact number limits for each grade, and we found those numbers in the official published rule.
Thick solid wood panels are officially grade D, which is in the lower half.
UK guidance says walls and ceilings in normal rooms should be grade C and in corridors grade B, so bare wood there usually needs a fire-protecting treatment or covering.

glossary.reaction to fire: How much a material itself adds to a fire when it is heated or lit.
glossary.Euroclass: The European grade A1, A2, B, C, D, E or F for reaction to fire; A1 is best.
glossary.EN 13501-1: The European standard that sets out how test results are turned into a Euroclass.
glossary.SBI (EN 13823): Single Burning Item test: a burner in a corner made of the material, with the heat and smoke measured for about 20 minutes.
glossary.FIGRA: Fire growth rate index, in watts per second: how fast the fire's heat output climbs. Lower is safer.
glossary.THR600s: Total heat released in the first 600 seconds (10 minutes) of the SBI test, in megajoules.
glossary.LFS: Lateral flame spread: whether flames travel sideways to the edge of the test panel.
glossary.EN ISO 11925-2: Small-flame test: a match-sized flame is held on the material for 15 or 30 seconds.
glossary.Fs: How far the flame climbs up the sample in the small-flame test, in millimetres.
glossary.EN ISO 1182: Furnace test for whether a material burns at all (temperature rise, mass loss, flaming time).
glossary.EN ISO 1716 / PCS: Test that burns a sample completely to measure the total heat it could give off (gross calorific potential), in MJ/kg or MJ/m2.
glossary.SMOGRA: Smoke growth rate: how fast smoke production rises in the SBI test.
glossary.TSP600s: Total smoke produced in the first 600 seconds of the SBI test.
glossary.s1, s2, s3: Smoke grades; s1 is least smoke, s3 means no limit.
glossary.d0, d1, d2: Burning-droplet grades; d0 means none, d2 means no limit.
glossary.lining: The surface material on a wall or ceiling that faces into the room.
glossary.circulation space: Corridors, lobbies and stairs that people use to move around and escape.
glossary.Approved Document B: The UK government's official guidance on meeting the fire-safety part of the Building Regulations in England.
glossary.Classification Without Further Testing (: An official list of products given a fire grade by law so each maker need not re-test.
glossary.cross-laminated timber (CLT): Thick panels made by gluing layers of boards at right angles.
glossary.laminated veneer lumber (LVL): Beams or panels made by gluing many thin sheets of wood together.
glossary.cone calorimeter (ISO 5660): A bench test that heats a small square sample under a cone-shaped heater and measures the heat released.
glossary.bio-based: Made from plants or other living material, such as wood.
glossary.fire-retardant treatment: A chemical soak or coating that makes a material harder to burn.
glossary.DFL-s1: A flooring fire grade (D for floors) with the lowest smoke grade.

recommendations: Before any number goes into a nanopublication, open the 2016/364 annex (EUR-Lex PDF or legislation.gov.uk) and check Table 1 character by character; my copy came through a summariser.

Use class C (FIGRA <= 250 W/s, THR600s <= 15 MJ) and class B (FIGRA <= 120 W/s, THR600s <= 7.5 MJ) as the two design targets for a bio-based lining; class D (FIGRA <= 750 W/s) is the untreated-timber baseline.
Do not state cone-calorimeter (ISO 5660) thresholds as EU or UK regulatory limits; the Euroclass system does not use that test.
Read the standards list at the back of Approved Document B (around line 10282 of adb2.txt) to get the cited BS EN 13501-1 edition and the 2029 change.
